title: Assessment Mnemonics
body:
## History

| Mnemonic | Expansion |
|---|---|
| **SAMPLE** | Signs/symptoms, Allergies, Medications, Past medical history, Last oral intake, Events leading up |
| **OPQRST** | Onset, Provocation/palliation, Quality, Region/radiation, Severity (`0–10`), Time |
| **AEIOU-TIPS** (altered mental status) | Alcohol, Epilepsy/electrolytes, Insulin (high or low glucose), Opiates/overdose, Uremia, Trauma/temperature, Infection, Psychiatric/poisoning, Stroke/shock/seizure |

## Physical exam

| Mnemonic | Expansion |
|---|---|
| **XABCDE** | eXsanguinating hemorrhage, Airway, Breathing, Circulation, Disability (GCS/pupils/glucose), Exposure + Environment |
| **DCAP-BTLS** | Deformities, Contusions, Abrasions, Punctures/penetrations, Burns, Tenderness, Lacerations, Swelling |
| **AVPU** | Alert, responds to Verbal, responds to Pain, Unresponsive |
| **PMS / CMS** | Pulse, Motor, Sensation — check distal to every splint before and after (CMS = Circulation, Motor, Sensation, same thing) |
| **5 Ps** (compartment syndrome / neurovascular) | Pain out of proportion, Pallor, Paresthesia, Pulselessness, Paralysis (some add Poikilothermia) |

## Stroke

| Mnemonic | Expansion |
|---|---|
| **BE-FAST** | Balance loss, Eyes (vision change), Face droop, Arm drift, Speech change, Time last known well |
| **Cincinnati Prehospital Stroke Scale** | Three items only: facial droop, arm drift, abnormal speech. Any one abnormal gives roughly a `72%` chance of stroke |

> **Key:** "Time last known well" beats "time found down." Thrombolytic and thrombectomy windows are measured from the last normal moment.

## Handoff

| Mnemonic | Expansion |
|---|---|
| **MIST** (trauma) | Mechanism, Injuries found/suspected, Signs (vitals + trend), Treatment given |
| **SBAR** | Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation |

## Triage

| Mnemonic | Expansion |
|---|---|
| **START RPM** (adults) | Respirations (over `30` = red), Perfusion (radial pulse absent or cap refill over `2 s` = red), Mental status (cannot follow simple commands = red). Walking wounded = green; not breathing after airway opened = black |
| **JumpSTART** (peds 1–8 y) | Same idea, RR limits `15–45`, and an apneic child with a pulse gets `5` rescue breaths before being tagged black |

## Toxicology

| Mnemonic | Expansion |
|---|---|
| **SLUDGEM** (cholinergic / organophosphate) | Salivation, Lacrimation, Urination, Defecation, Gastric upset, Emesis, Miosis |
| **DUMBELS** (same toxidrome) | Defecation/diaphoresis, Urination, Miosis, Bradycardia/bronchorrhea/bronchospasm, Emesis, Lacrimation, Salivation |
| **MUDPILES** (high anion gap acidosis) | Methanol, Uremia, Diabetic ketoacidosis, Propylene glycol, Iron/Isoniazid, Lactate, Ethylene glycol, Salicylates |

> **Trap:** The killers in the cholinergic toxidrome are the three Bs — bronchorrhea, bronchospasm, bradycardia — not the wet clothes.

## Reversible causes of arrest

| H's | T's |
|---|---|
| Hypovolemia | Tension pneumothorax |
| Hypoxia | Tamponade (cardiac) |
| Hydrogen ion (acidosis) | Toxins |
| Hypo-/hyperkalemia | Thrombosis, pulmonary |
| Hypothermia | Thrombosis, coronary |

Hypoglycemia is often taught as a sixth H; AHA folds it under toxins/metabolic. Run the list out loud during every pulse check.
